thread:
dan: Promo stalled for ai-ingress chart v2.5.0 -> staging. deploy-bot shows postop hook 'apply-configs' failed due to ConfigMap version mismatch and hook executed before new configmap was created. Anyone else seeing the hook ordering fail?

deploy-bot: promote-blocked: helm-hook-failure apply-configs (post-install), reason=failed to apply config: ConfigMap 'ai-ingress-config' not found at expected version v42; action=hold. logs: kubectl -n staging logs job/helm-hook-apply-configs-1777770001

anya: I see it. The chart introduced a post-install hook that patches a configmap using .Files.Get and expects the new configmap generated by the template (which uses a computed hash). But helm sometimes runs post-install hooks before chart objects are fully available in cluster due to ordering when using hooks + CRD-like resources.

mike: weird — we've templated the config into a separate manifest (ConfigMap) in same release. Hook should see it. Did we change post-renderer or helm flags?

sophia: we added a pre-upgrade annotation in the release pipeline yesterday to split manifests across batches to reduce memory pressure. That might have introduced a timing window where the hook job executed while the configmap was still being created by a later batch.

dan: options: 1) patch the hook to retry/wait for configmap availability (fast hotfix to chart -> canary re-promote), 2) pin staging to previous chart 2.4.3 and abort promote (safe), 3) revert the batch-split in the pipeline and re-run promote (requires CI change).

anya: patching the hook to implement a short wait-and-retry (with a 60s backoff and 5 retries) seems low risk and quick. We should also add a helm test that validates hook ordering.

mike: agree for staging, but for prod we may prefer a pin to avoid silent ordering flakiness. If we hotpatch chart we must ensure the change lands before prod promo.

sophia: I'll revert the pipeline split in a branch to test if that removes the race, but that'll take a bit. For immediate unblocking, hotpatch the hook.

deploy-bot: suggested_action=hotpatch_chart, user=sophia, patch_description="add wait-for-configmap loop to apply-configs hook", timestamp=1777770018

dan: go ahead with hotpatch on canary and re-promote. Keep release pinned only if canary still fails after hotpatch. Also add release-note fragment about the ordering race and the mitigation.

anya: creating PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/601 - adds a small init loop to hook job:
```
# /bin/sh -c
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  if kubectl -n staging get configmap ai-ingress-config -o name; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
# then apply patch
```

mike: I applied a temporary hotpatch to the canary hook (kubectl -n staging apply -f hotpatch-hook.yaml) and restarted the hook job. Observing logs now: job completed and canary progressed to healthy.

sophia: adding release note: "Staging canary blocked due to helm post-install hook running before a templated ConfigMap was available. Temporary hotpatch added to retry; follow-up to add hook stability check and revert pipeline split."

dan: audit commands I ran:
```
# inspect hook logs
kubectl -n staging logs job/helm-hook-apply-configs-1777770001
# patch hook (hotpatch)
kubectl -n staging apply -f hotpatch-hook.yaml
# confirm canary rollout status
kubectl -n staging rollout status deployment/ai-ingress-canary
# annotate release with pin/hotpatch info
kubectl -n releases annotate release ai-ingress promoted-by=dan hotpatch=1777770018
```

deploy-bot: action=hotpatch_applied, user=dan, target=canary, patch_ref=PR#601, timestamp=1777770026

dan: leaving promo resumed note and linking PR. we'll leave the staging promo unpinned since hotpatch passed, but schedule a follow-up to remove the temporary retry and fix ordering safely in the chart/pipeline. :white_check_mark:
